messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — CI started failing for the new attention kernels when we enable LTO + nvcc on the ptx arch matrix. Build passes locally for me if I disable LTO, but CI artifacts are ~3x bigger and the runner OOMs. Anyone seen this?

oliver: Ugh. Probably the linker pulling in host-side LTO symbols into fatbins. Did you see the nvcc commandline in the logs?

maria: Yep, snippet from the job: `nvcc -O3 -gencode=arch=compute_80,code=sm_80 -Xcompiler -fPIC -flto -fuse-linker-plugin -rdc=true -lineinfo -o libkernels.so` — CI adds `-flto` globally via the toolchain.

anya: That combo is sketchy. NVCC's device code and the host LTO flow don't play nicely. Historically we used `-Xcompiler -fno-lto` or build device objects separately then link host with LTO.

oliver: Agreed. Two approaches: 1) disable host LTO for nvcc compile units (`-Xcompiler -fno-lto`) and keep LTO for pure host C++; 2) split build so CUDA sources compile to cubin/ptx and archive + link later (no host LTO touching device objects).

maria: Option 2 sounds safe but CI build graph needs >1 step and our current monolithic job makes that awkward. Also the PTX in CI shows `ptxas` reporting big .o sizes. I ran `nvdisasm` on the artifact and there are duplicate kernels from generic/arch variants.

tj: Could be fatbin embedding multiple code entries (PTX + SASS) for all arch codes. Check `--generate-code` flags. If CI uses an expanded arch matrix (compute_70, 75, 80, 86) we end up embedding many variants. Consider narrowing arch list for the CI artifact and run full matrix in a separate release job.

maria: Good call. Current matrix is a result of the platform tests branch. Let's gate size-sensitive builds to `sm_80` only and run full multi-arch nightly.

anya: Also try `--relocatable-device-code=true` (`-rdc=true`) already present, but `-Xptxas -v` can show register/memory use. For size trimming: `-gencode=arch=compute_80,code=compute_80` to keep PTX-only, or `code=sm_80` for cubin. PTX+SASS duplicates increase size.

oliver: FYI stripping symbols helps: `cuobjdump --dump-sass` is useful for inspection, and `--strip` on fatbin? We usually run `nvcc --fatbin -otc` historically, but modern flow: use `cubin` outputs and run `objcopy --strip-unneeded` on the host archive. Need to be careful to not strip relocation metadata needed by runtime (rdc).

maria: The CI bot also shows warnings from `ptxas`: "Assembly size exceeds limit" for a few kernels. Maybe our new attention tiling kernel pushes ptxas over the heuristics and causes extra compilation artifacts.

tj: If ptxas rejects or changes optimization, you might see fallback to larger codegen. Try `-O2` vs `-O3` or `-ftz` changes. Also `-Xptxas -dlcm=ca` can alter codegen a bit. But don't guess — add a build step to capture `ptxas` verbose output: `-Xptxas -v` and upload to CI artifacts.

maria: I'll add that. Any opinion on enabling `-fno-exceptions`/`-fno-rtti` for device translation units to reduce metadata?

anya: Those help host binary size; device side not much effect. For device, prefer reducing duplicate specialization instantiations: control templates, avoid header-only huge metaprogramming in kernel headers.

oliver: Short-term plan I'm proposing for CI: (1) Add a separate job for CUDA builds with host-LTO disabled (`-Xcompiler -fno-lto`), (2) Limit arch matrix for fast PR CI (single sm target), (3) Collect `ptxas -v` and `nvdisasm` output as artifacts for failing jobs, (4) Run a nightly full-arch size/regression job that fails the build when fatbin > threshold.

maria: +1. Also let's add an explicit check that artifacts don't contain duplicate SASS for same kernel across arch codes. We can parse `cuobjdump --list` output and fail when duplicate names found.

tj: CI infra note: ccache/sccache only helps host compile. For nvcc we use ccache for host objects but device builds still expensive. Maybe use a build cache for prebuilt cubins keyed by nvcc flags + arch list. Could store in s3 and rehydrate in CI.

oliver: I'll prototype a caching step. For now, I'll adjust the job definitions and push a patch that sets `NVCC_FLAGS += -Xcompiler -fno-lto` for the CUDA job and reduces the matrix.

maria: Thanks. I'll add a follow-up RFC comment about separating host LTO and device object flows so this doesn't keep biting us.

ci-bot: Build 8421: cuda-kernels-cuda-80 (PR 1192) — started. Artifacts: https://ci.example/redwood/8421/artifacts (ptxas.log attached).

maria: nice — opening a PR with the CI changes now. I'll @oliver for infra review and @anya to sanity-check ptxas logs once uploaded. :shipit:
